FILES: rich/text.py:775-807 (Text.expand_tabs)
CAUSE: When expanding tabs, the method uses the default `self.style` for any additional spaces required to fill the tab stop, ignoring the specific style that might have been applied to the tab character itself.
FIX: Modify `Text.expand_tabs` to use the style of the `part` (the tab character) instead of `self.style` when appending the filling spaces.
REPRO: 
```python
from rich.text import Text
text = Text("Hello\tWorld", style="bold red")
text.stylize("underline green", 5, 6)
text.expand_tabs(tab_size=8)
# The expanded tab spaces (indices 6 and 7) should be "underline green", but are "bold red".
has_green_tab_extension = any("green" in str(span.style) and span.end > 6 for span in text._spans)
assert has_green_tab_extension, f"Tab extension lost the green style. Spans: {text._spans}"
```
